analysis.description: The paper proposes a knowledge distillation method to transfer the expertise of large language models (LLMs) to smaller language agents by sub-goal generation and execution, aiming at reducing computational costs while maintaining performance in complex tasks.

type.justification: The paper provides experimental results comparing their method with other approaches and includes performance evaluations across different tasks.
type.quote: Our approach demonstrates an overall performance of 65.43%, surpassing Swift-only by 16.71% (33.9% relative increase), and showing a slight improvement over SwiftSage of 3.3% (5.3% relative).

name.justification: The paper deals with decision-making agents and environments, commonly associated with reinforcement learning.
name.quote: The promising advantage of LLMs is attributed to their training on extensive text datasets, resulting in impressive capabilities. This prior knowledge can be leveraged for action planning to solve tasks in robotics and reinforcement learning.

name.justification: The research utilizes large language models and involves text-based environments, which are central to NLP.
name.quote: Recently, Large Language Models (LLMs) have found applications in various fields, including multi-task learning, decision making, answering questions, summarizing documents, translating languages, completing sentences.

name.justification: The paper specifically focuses on transferring knowledge from large models to smaller models using a method of knowledge distillation.
name.quote: One prevalent technique is the use of Knowledge Distillation (KD)... wherein a smaller model is trained with guidance from a larger model.

name.justification: The study involves leveraging large language models for guiding smaller models through knowledge distillation to generate sub-goals.
name.quote: While Large Language Models (LLMs) have demonstrated significant promise as agents in interactive tasks, their substantial computational requirements... constrain their practical utility.

is_contributed.justification: The study uses existing LLMs like ChatGPT and GPT-4, as mentioned in context of the research.
is_contributed.quote: Recent works have utilized in-context learning with LLMs to provide actions in autonomous decision-making agents and interactive environments.

is_executed.justification: The paper refers to using LLMs for annotation of expert trajectories, implying they were executed as part of the research.
is_executed.quote: We leverage an LLM to annotate an oracle path with a sequence of sub-goals towards completing a goal.

is_compared.justification: The research includes comparisons of their method involving LLMs with other methods in terms of performance.
is_compared.quote: Our approach demonstrates an overall performance of 65.43%... showing a slight improvement over SwiftSage.
